name: SBI Clerk (Junior Associate)
tagline: Junior Associate (Customer Support & Sales) at SBI: a state-wise exam with merit decided by Mains alone

overview.about: SBI recruits Junior Associates (Customer Support & Sales) state-wise through an online Prelims and Mains, followed by a test of the local language. There is no interview; the final merit list is based on Mains marks only.
eligibility: Graduation in any discipline (final-year students may apply provisionally as per the notification)
Age 20–28 years on the date fixed in the notification; relaxation: SC/ST 5 yrs, OBC-NCL 3 yrs, PwBD 10 yrs
Proficiency (read, write, speak, understand) in the official local language of the state applied for
A candidate can apply for vacancies in one state only

pattern.note: Separate timing per section; −0.25 per wrong answer
Category-wise cut-off; marks not added to final merit
Qualifying; exempt if the language was studied in Class 10 or 12 (with proof)

topics.t: Number system — divisibility, HCF & LCM, remainders, unit digits
Number series — missing number, wrong number, new-pattern (all types)
Data interpretation — table, bar, line, pie, radar & mixed charts
Caselet DI, missing DI & arithmetic DI

Vocabulary — synonyms, antonyms, idioms & phrasal verbs

cards.title: Mains decides everything
cards.body: Prelims only shortlists. Your **final rank = Mains marks** (out of 200), subject to clearing the local language test. Two candidates with equal Prelims scores can end up far apart in the final list.

cards.title: State-wise competition
cards.body: Vacancies and cut-offs are **state-wise and category-wise**. States with many applicants and few posts have higher cut-offs. Choose a state whose local language you know well; you cannot switch later.

cards.title: Prelims time plan
cards.body: Each section has a fixed 20 minutes. In Numerical Ability, finish simplification/approximation and number series first (about 10 Q in 6 minutes), then arithmetic, then DI. In Reasoning, do inequality, syllogism and coding before puzzles.

cards.title: Mains marks per minute
cards.body: GA gives **50 marks in 35 minutes**, the best return in the paper. Reasoning & Computer has **60 marks**; computer questions are quick, so attempt them first in that section.

cards.title: Junior Associate role
cards.body: Customer Support & Sales: cash, account opening, KYC, cross-selling of products, and digital banking support. Knowing SBI's products (YONO, savings schemes) helps in both GA and the job.

cards.q: SBI Clerk final merit is based on:
cards.explain: There is no interview; final selection is on Mains marks (after qualifying the local language test).

cards.q: In SBI Clerk Mains, which section carries 60 marks?
cards.explain: Reasoning & Computer Aptitude has 50 questions for 60 marks.

notes.p:
SBI recruits **Junior Associates (Customer Support & Sales)** through a **Prelims**, a **Mains** and a **Local Language Proficiency Test (LLPT)**. There is **no interview**. Prelims only shortlists candidates; the **final merit is based on Mains marks (out of 200)**, provided you clear the language test.

Selection is **state-wise and category-wise**: you compete only with candidates who applied for the same state and category.
points: Prelims: qualifying; three sections with fixed 20-minute timers.
Mains: General/Financial Awareness, General English, Quantitative Aptitude, Reasoning & Computer Aptitude; 200 marks.
LLPT: qualifying; failing it cancels selection.
Negative marking: ¼ of the question's marks for each wrong answer.

notes.p:
Mains structure (as in recent notifications; check the current one): **General/Financial Awareness 50 Q, 50 marks, 35 min**; **General English 40 Q, 40 marks, 35 min**; **Quantitative Aptitude 50 Q, 50 marks, 45 min**; **Reasoning & Computer Aptitude 50 Q, 60 marks, 45 min**.

**Worked example: where is time most valuable?**
GA: 50 marks ÷ 35 min ≈ **1.43 marks per minute**.
English: 40 ÷ 35 ≈ **1.14**.
Quant: 50 ÷ 45 ≈ **1.11**.
Reasoning & Computer: 60 ÷ 45 ≈ **1.33**.
GA gives the highest return, and its questions take seconds each if you have revised well. Reasoning & Computer is next; computer questions are quick, so do them first in that section.
Each Prelims section has a fixed 20 minutes; unused time is lost.
points: **Numerical Ability:** simplification/approximation and series first (about 10 questions in 6 minutes), then arithmetic word problems, then DI.
**Reasoning:** inequality, syllogism, coding and direction/blood relations first; then puzzles.
**English:** error spotting and fillers are quick; RC can take longer, so time it in mocks.
Clerk cut-offs are high, so **accuracy above 90%** matters more than attempting every question.

notes.p: Vacancies and cut-offs differ by state. A state with few posts and many applicants usually has a higher cut-off. But the deciding factor must be **language**: you must be able to read, write, speak and understand the state's official language, or you will be disqualified at the LLPT even after clearing Mains.
points: Check past state-wise cut-offs on the SBI careers page.
Choose a state whose language you know well; you cannot change later.
Keep Class 10/12 language certificates ready if you studied it in school.
Treating Prelims as the main exam and starting Mains GA too late.
Choosing a state for a lower cut-off without knowing its language.
Attempting difficult puzzles first in a 20-minute section.
Guessing blindly in the last minute.
Ignoring SBI-specific products (YONO, schemes) that appear in GA and help on the job.
No interview; Mains (200) decides merit.
LLPT is qualifying.
State-wise and category-wise selection.
Mains GA: best marks per minute.
Reasoning & Computer: 60 marks; do computer questions first.
Prelims accuracy 90%+.

cards.title: What it is
cards.body: After Mains, candidates must show they can **read, write, speak and understand** the official local language of the state they applied for. It is **qualifying**: failing it means no selection, whatever your Mains score.

cards.title: Who is exempt
cards.body: Candidates who studied the specified local language in **Class 10 or Class 12** and submit the mark sheet/certificate are exempt. Others take the test after provisional selection.

cards.title: How to prepare
cards.body: Practise reading aloud short passages (newspaper, bank forms), writing a few sentences, and a simple conversation on banking topics such as opening an account or depositing cash. Customer-facing vocabulary matters most.

cards.title: Why it exists
cards.body: Junior Associates deal directly with local customers, often in rural and semi-urban branches. The test ensures they can serve customers in their own language.

cards.title: Choose the state wisely
cards.body: If you are not fluent in a state's language, a lower cut-off there is a false bargain: you may clear Mains and still be disqualified at the language test.

cards.q: Who is exempt from SBI Clerk's local language test?
options: Candidates with a degree in English
Candidates who studied the language in Class 10 or 12 (with proof)
cards.explain: Proof of studying the local language in Class 10 or 12 exempts the candidate.
It is a qualifying test; it carries no merit marks.

notes.p:
After Mains, SBI checks that each provisionally selected candidate can **read, write, speak and understand** the **official local language** of the state they applied for. The test is **qualifying**: it adds no marks, but failing it means **no appointment**, whatever your Mains score.

The reason is practical. Junior Associates work at the counter in urban, semi-urban and rural branches, opening accounts, handling cash and solving customer problems. Many customers prefer or only speak the local language.

Candidates who have **studied the specified local language in Class 10 or Class 12** and can show the **mark sheet or certificate** are exempt from the test. All others take the test after provisional selection. Check the notification for the exact list of languages for each state and the documents accepted.
points: Keep the original mark sheet and a self-attested copy ready.
The language must appear as a subject on the mark sheet.
If your state has more than one official language listed, any one listed language usually suffices; confirm in the notification.

notes.h: How the test is usually conducted
notes.p: The format can vary, but candidates typically face simple tasks rather than a literature exam.
points: **Reading:** read aloud a short passage, a notice or a bank form.
**Writing:** write a few sentences about yourself or a short application.
**Speaking and listening:** a short conversation on a banking situation such as opening an account, depositing cash or asking about a loan.
Clarity and confidence matter more than perfect grammar.

notes.p:
If you know the language but are out of practice, structured practice for a month is usually enough.

**Week 1:** read a local-language newspaper for 15 minutes daily; note banking words (account, deposit, withdrawal, interest, loan, cheque).
**Week 2:** write 5–6 sentences daily about yourself and your daily routine.
**Week 3:** role-play customer conversations with a friend or family member: account opening, ATM card issue, passbook update.
**Week 4:** read bank forms and notices aloud; practise filling a deposit slip in the local language.

**Example dialogue to practise:** customer asks how to open a savings account → you list documents (Aadhaar, PAN, photograph), explain the minimum balance rules and offer to help fill the form.

points: Choosing a state for its lower cut-off without knowing its language.
Assuming spoken fluency is enough; reading and writing are also tested.
Forgetting to carry the Class 10/12 certificate for exemption.
Not practising banking vocabulary in the local language.
LLPT: read, write, speak, understand.
Qualifying only; failing = no selection.
Exempt if the language was studied in Class 10 or 12 (with proof).
Practise customer conversations and form reading.
Choose your state by language first, cut-off second.
